title: Test ID - 39 Compiler Test 1 - 2026
series: GATE 2026 Test Series - Computer Science Engineering

questions.html:
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

 

(a) Under static scoping, the output for init(1) is 7 -3.

(b) Under static scoping, the output for init (1) is 9 -5.

(c) Under dynamic scoping, the output for init (1) is 5 -2.

(d) Under dynamic scoping, the output for init (1) is 7 -5.
questions.solution:
Answer: (a, c)

Solution:

Static scoping trace (init (1))

init: set a=1, b=-1, then T() → a=3, b=-2.
a>=b true → call H:

·         In H: local b = a+1 = 4.

·         Call G:

o    In G: local a = b-1 = -3 (uses global b=-2).

o    Call F:

§  T() → global a=5, b=-3

§  a<b? 5<-3 no → b+=3 → global b=0

o    a+=4 (local a becomes 1; globals unchanged)

o    b-=2 → global b=-2

·         Back to H: call T() → global a=7, b=-3
Prints: 7 -3

Dynamic scoping trace (init (1))

init: a=1, b=-1, then T() → a=3, b=-2.
a>=b true → call H:

·         In H: local b = a+1 = 4 (a is global here).

·         Call G:

o    In G: local a = b-1 = 3 (uses H’s local b=4).

o    Call F:

§  T() → acts on G.a and H.b: G.a=5, H.b=3

§  a<b? 5<3 no → b+=3 → H.b=6

o    Back to G: a+=4 → G.a=9; b-=2 → H.b=4

·         Back to H: call T() → a is global (no local), b is H’s local:

o    global a=5, H.b=3
Prints: 5 -2 (global b stayed at -2)

Correct options

(a) True — static scoping with init (1) prints 7 -3.

(b) False — that’s not the static result for init (1).

(c) True — dynamic scoping with init (1) prints 5 -2.

(d) False — dynamic does not print 7 -5 for init (1).
